\section{Gaussian Space --- Normalized Blocks}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.NormalizedBlocks
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Normalized Blocks: Introduction}
Convergence against scalar Lipschitz tests passes to bounded continuous tests of finite products of probability laws. In particular, independent normalized Boolean blocks converge to a standard Gaussian vector.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Normalized Blocks: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Product convergence from scalar Lipschitz convergence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_pi_of_scalar_lipschitz}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\mu_m)_{m\ge0}$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on $\mathbb R$. Suppose that for
every $c\ge0$ and every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
$\int\psi\,d\mu_m\to\int\psi\,d\nu$ as $m\to\infty$. Then, for every $n\ge0$ and bounded
continuous $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, $\int F\,d\mu_m^{\otimes n}\to\int
F\,d\nu^{\otimes n}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Normalized Boolean sum law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolSumLaw}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
For $m\ge0$, let $\nu_m$ be the probability law of $(m+1)^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{m+1}\epsilon_j$, where the $\epsilon_j$ are independent uniform signs in $\{-1,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian limit for products of normalized sum laws]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolSum_pi}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolSumLaw, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolSum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_pi_of_scalar_lipschitz, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, and for each $m\ge0$ let $\nu_m$ be the law of $(m+1)^{-1/2}$ times the sum
of $m+1$ independent uniform signs. For every bounded continuous $F:\mathbb
R^n\to\mathbb R$, $\int F\,d\nu_m^{\otimes n}\to\int F\,d\gamma_n$ as $m\to\infty$,
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian limit for normalized Boolean blocks]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolBlocks}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolSumLaw, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolSum_pi, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$ and let $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and continuous. For each
$m\ge0$, take independent uniform signs $\varepsilon_{ij}\in\{-1,1\}$, with $1\le i\le
n$ and $1\le j\le m+1$, and set $S_m(i)=(m+1)^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{m+1}\varepsilon_{ij}$.
Then $\mathbb E[F(S_m)]\to\int F\,d\gamma_n$ as $m\to\infty$, where $\gamma_n$ is
standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}
